question: Known as the 'sorrow of Bihar', the river _______ causes great destruction due to its frequently changing course.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Kosi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kosi River is known as the "sorrow of Bihar" because of its frequent flooding and changing course, which causes great destruction in the state
 
• The Kosi River's annual floods damage agricultural land and destroy the rural economy.
 
• During the monsoon season, the river's water flow increases up to 18 times.
 
• The Kosi River is highly sedimented and has many intersecting channels that shift laterally, causing floods.
 
• In 2005, 95% of the river's water shifted into a channel it hadn't used in over 100 years.
 
• The Kosi River carries large amounts of silt during the monsoon season, which contributes to its instability.
 
• The upper course of the river produces one of the highest silt yields in the world.
 
• The Kosi River originates in Tibet and flows through China, Nepal, and India before depositing itself into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• It is one of the largest tributaries of the Ganges.

• Subarnarekha River
 
 
• The Subarnarekha River originates from the Ranchi Plateau in Jharkhand, India.
 
• It flows through the states of Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This river is approximately 395 kilometers long and serves as a vital water source for the regions it passes through.
 
 
 
• Indravati River
 
 
• The Indravati River originates from the Dandakaranya range and flows into the Godavari River.
 
• It traverses through the states of Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, and Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• Brahmani River
 
 
• The Brahmani River is a major river in the state of Odisha.
 
• It is formed by the confluence of the Shankh and South Koel rivers.
